limiterDetail: The main limiter is a combination of current and wind. Tara, Decabaitot, Alava and Turda run 1.3–1.7 kt now and build to 1.7–2.0 kt around 4–6 PM. ECMWF wind is 11–15 kt now (gusts 17–20), easing to 7–10 kt across most grounds by 9 PM. Rain is negligible today.

pagasa.detail: PAGASA: no gale, wind signal or heavy-rain warning for Calamian / MIMAROPA. Latest: Tropical Cyclone Warning, Super Typhoon Rosal (Champi) Signal #2 and Signal #1, Thu 22 Oct 10:48 AM PHT, for the far north only. The only other recent item is a Cagayan Valley flood advisory (5:11 AM), which does not cover Palawan. This morning's PAGASA outlook flagged strong to gale-force gusts for most of Luzon and Visayas today and Fri 23.

changed.title: ⚠️ What changed since this morning
items: No material change: today is still the POOR day. The grounds snapshot moved from 0 GOOD / 9 MARGINAL / 4 POOR / 3 VERY POOR to 0 GOOD / 8 MARGINAL / 6 POOR / 2 VERY POOR. Alava eased to POOR (1.3 kt), while Nangalao dropped to POOR on 14.6 kt wind with gusts to 20. Tara (1.7 kt) and Decabaitot (1.6 kt) stay VERY POOR, and the afternoon current build peaks around 4–6 PM.

Supply timing is unchanged: arrivals thin out on Fri 23 from today's weak catch, then recover over the weekend. Friday is still MARGINAL (9.7 kt, gusts 15) but now carries a little light rain (~1.7 mm). Sun 25 is still the calmest day (4.1 kt). PAGASA kept Signal #2 on Super Typhoon Rosal for the far north only (10:48 AM PHT); nothing for Palawan.

bestWindow.headline: Tonight about 9 PM–1 AM, then Friday about 8 AM–1 PM (Coron side)
details: 9 PM–1 AM tonight: Coron and Galoc on 0.3 kt current and 7 kt wind, dry. Panlaitan and Maglalambay 0.3 kt but 9–10 kt wind. Linapacan 0.4 kt with wind down to 6 kt.
8 AM–1 PM Friday: Coron, Galoc and Maglalambay 0.2–0.3 kt, Linapacan 0.2–0.3 kt, wind 7–9 kt on the Coron side, light drizzle (0.2 mm/h) until about 10 AM. Ciron is best earlier, 3–9 AM at 0.2 kt.
Keep boats off Tara and Decabaitot all 24h, and off Turda and Alava this afternoon. Avoid the 4–6 PM current peak everywhere in the south and west.
